response:
It takes a lot of courage to recognize how your past trauma is affecting your present behavior. It is completely understandable to feel terrified at the thought of being a single parent, but begging someone to return to an unhappy dynamic won't heal the underlying pain for either of you, or create a healthy environment for your son. 

The most important step you can take right now is to seek professional support. A therapist or counselor can help you process the childhood abuse you endured, learn healthier ways to cope with those deep wounds, and break the cycle of abusive behavior. Working on your own healing is the best way to build a safe, stable future for both you and your son, whether you are co-parenting or navigating life on your own.
